From f32f19339596b214c208c0dba716f4b6cc4f6958 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2020 06:38:07 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] bonding: set dev->needed_headroom in bond_setup_by_slave()

syzbot managed to crash a host by creating a bond
with a GRE device.

For non Ethernet device, bonding calls bond_setup_by_slave()
instead of ether_setup(), and unfortunately dev->needed_headroom
was not copied from the new added member.

[  171.243095] skbuff: skb_under_panic: text:ffffffffa184b9ea len:116 put:20 head:ffff883f84012dc0 data:ffff883f84012dbc tail:0x70 end:0xd00 dev:bond0
[  171.243111] 
diff --git a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
index 42ef25ec0af5..14740d3053b8 100644
--- a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
@@ -1315,6 +1315,7 @@ static void bond_setup_by_slave(struct net_device *bond_dev,
 
 	bond_dev->type		    = slave_dev->type;
 	bond_dev->hard_header_len   = slave_dev->hard_header_len;
+	bond_dev->needed_headroom   = slave_dev->needed_headroom;
 	bond_dev->addr_len	    = slave_dev->addr_len;
 
 	memcpy(bond_dev->broadcast, slave_dev->broadcast,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c`**
- A new line was added to the `bond_setup_by_slave` function:
  ```c
  bond_dev->needed_headroom = slave_dev->needed_headroom;
  ```
  This line copies the `needed_headroom` value from the `slave_dev` to the `bond_dev`.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a bug where the `needed_headroom` property was not being set for the bonding device when it was created from a non-Ethernet device. By copying this property from the `slave_dev`, the patch ensures that the bonding device has the correct buffer space allocated, preventing potential crashes (as reported by syzbot) when using bonding with GRE devices. This change enhances the stability and correctness of the bonding functionality in the network driver.

Fixes: f5184d267c1a ("net: Allow netdevices to specify needed head/tailroom")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Reported-by: syzbot <syzkaller@googlegroups.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `bond_setup_by_slave` function not copying the `needed_headroom` value from the `slave_dev` to the `bond_dev`. This omission led to insufficient buffer space being allocated for the bonding device, which could result in memory corruption and crashes when handling packets, particularly with non-Ethernet devices like GRE.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void bond_setup_by_slave(struct net_device *bond_dev,
 				struct net_device *slave_dev)
 {
 	bond_dev->header_ops	    = slave_dev->header_ops;
 
 	bond_dev->type		    = slave_dev->type;
 	bond_dev->hard_header_len   = slave_dev->hard_header_len;
+	bond_dev->needed_headroom   = slave_dev->needed_headroom;
 	bond_dev->addr_len	    = slave_dev->addr_len;
 
 	memcpy(bond_dev->broadcast, slave_dev->broadcast,
 		slave_dev->addr_len);
 }

This omission results in the bonding device not having sufficient buffer space for packet processing, leading to potential memory corruption and crashes, especially when handling non-Ethernet devices like GRE.

bond_dev->needed_headroom = slave_dev->needed_headroom;
